subject.title: [codex] acknowledge terminal Gmail OAuth watch failures

question: Should a terminal Gmail OAuth failure retain durable pending work for automatic post-reauth catch-up, rather than relying on a later Gmail notification to replay the missed history?
rationale: The implementation must balance avoiding unbounded Pub/Sub retries against the watch contract for delivery recovery; choosing whether recovery is automatic, explicitly operator-triggered, or intentionally best-effort is a product and operational contract decision.

options.title: Require automatic catch-up
options.body: Persist enough pending state or add a deterministic recovery trigger so re-authentication processes the unhandled history before the delivery is considered safely complete.

options.title: Keep best-effort replay
options.body: Accept that acknowledged notifications are only recovered after a later Gmail update and document that potential delivery gap explicitly.

recommendation.title: Require automatic catch-up
recommendation.body: Persist enough pending state or add a deterministic recovery trigger so re-authentication processes the unhandled history before the delivery is considered safely complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent Gmail-watch history candidate from the supplied release provenance.
